node_model.purpose: Relationship-first semantic graph. Nodes describe ownership, state layer, service boundary, or subsystem; byte layouts and wire schemas are not copied.

evidence_levels.VERIFIED: Direct pinned SDK/Ghidra layout, committed implementation, test, or explicit artifact evidence; not runtime observation by itself.
evidence_levels.SUPPORTED: Multiple static artifacts or bounded bodies support the relationship without a runtime oracle.
evidence_levels.OBSERVED_CURRENT: Current OpenSpore source or test behavior; comparison-only for the original game.
evidence_levels.INFERRED: Analytical composition or narrow semantic interpretation.
evidence_levels.UNKNOWN: The available evidence does not establish the claim.

operation_model.create: Construct or materialize a definition, reference, object, or service state.
operation_model.query: Resolve, enumerate, lookup, or select a value without implying mutation.
operation_model.mutate: Change live, configuration, authored, relationship, economy, or presentation state.
operation_model.serialize: Read/write a value or state through an explicit codec boundary; layout presence alone is not a write claim.
operation_model.destroy: Release, clear, unregister, dispose, or return a live object/resource to an owner.

node_model.sorting: Arrays are sorted by stable id or structure_id; source_refs are sorted by path then locator.

edges.description: The content record is addressed by the full resource identity; no name/path is embedded in the DBPF row.
Registered packed/directory databases index records and expose identity/extent metadata.
A requested key enters the manager's database/factory/cache lookup path.
Registry state dispatches the operational load path; exact manager ordering remains inferred.
Typed load results are retained/released through typed reference and resource caches.
Lazy Cell references resolve record bytes and direct Cell templates, not runtime state.
Cell content includes globals, world, populate, and scale/advect composition references.
Resolved Cell templates and model keys feed live Cell pool/state construction; placement and full selection are bounded.
Cell runtime selects current/background world, scale-banded level, and advect state.
Live transforms, model keys, animations, health, and GFX indices project into presentation state.
Gameplay mutations, interactions, animation/effect requests, and UI projections have event-like state consequences, but the original event ABI is unresolved.
Presentation worlds, meshes, textures, effects, and UI consume model/material/texture assets.
CreatureData contains ordered rigblock/part definitions.
Rigblock model group/instance references resolve to model or derived presentation identity; exact conversion is bounded.
EditorData composite separates persistent authored core from transient editor shell/history/pose state.
Editor input/tools mutate part, hierarchy, color, and paint state.
Rigblocks are converted to derived editor skin meshes/materials.
Live creature state carries ability/evolution/avatar progression relationships.
SpaceData composition owns/generated star and planet records and their databases.
SpaceData includes empire registry, active context, colonies, trade, mission, and inventory state.
Generated planet records and terrain identity are resolved into live planet and star/space state.
Empire political IDs are the identity key for relationship map entries and transition state.
War/peace/alliance/delta transitions feed communication or message state, but exact event payloads are unresolved.
Space session composes mission manager and tracked mission state.
Mission rewards, tools, costs, and deliverables relate to inventory/trade/economy state; exact payout order is unresolved.
Noun/factory registry materializes registered creature game-data instances.
Live city/building/terrain spatial/model state is consumed by renderer/UI presentation, while gameplay/layout state remains separate.
Domain events can be queued or dispatched through message infrastructure, but not every event variant uses it.
Mode and editor listeners receive messages that coordinate entry, exit, display, and mode transitions.
Configuration options, collectable config, scripts, and property lists share the typed property substrate.
Collectable/configuration property values can configure content and fallback behavior, but not every Cell field is bound.
Editor property-backed configuration, template, palette, and validation policies are a separate configuration consumer.
PropertyList is a shared serialization substrate; exact parent inclusion and outer framing are unknown.
Cell serializable state is a mode-specific save candidate inside the composite persistence service; exact codec is unresolved.
Load context and mode/save headers can select or restore a mode, but exact LoadGame dispatch and state survival are unknown.
Cell mode owns and initializes Cell gameplay and presentation state through mode callbacks.
Space mode owns active-space session, missions, inventory, and planet/empire context.
Mode entry/exit activates, restores, or releases presentation worlds/UI/editor state.
PresentationData references model, texture, material, skin, world, and UI assets for decoding and binding; assets do not own gameplay state.
Editor skin meshes/materials/textures are derived presentation output and not gameplay selectors.
Empire UFO/captain keys and species/profile references can select presentation assets; actual asset use is not established.
Creature, Cell, unlock, and mission progression candidates reference resource identities, but exact resolution paths differ by owner.
Queued messages dispatch listeners and domain events, but queue records and event records remain distinct schemas.
Bounded model/material/texture decoders and binding surfaces feed presentation state; no complete original presentation asset writer or wire schema is recovered.
Material/editor/configuration properties can participate in presentation definitions, but runtime and wire ownership is unresolved.
Mission/economy reward and unlock relationships are candidate progression inputs; exact settlement and grant order is unresolved.
Serializable cGameData/noun owners can be represented through the persistence service, but object pointer restoration is unresolved.
Presentation is a projection/owner of draw state and must not be treated as the source of gameplay collision, health, or progression.

flows.description: A DBPF identity enters the resource registry, is read/decompressed, decoded or cached, and becomes a runtime resource/model/content object that presentation can bind. Exact original load order is inferred where noted.

steps.action: Resolve complete type/group/instance identity.
Select database/factory/cache and obtain record/runtime object.
Retain typed object or bounded host value.
Bind model/material/texture/world state or derived host handle.

flows.description: Cell content references resolve into Cell runtime entities; movement, combat, eat, animation, effect, and UI state produce event-like consequences and presentation projections. The original event transport remains unresolved.

steps.action: Decode world/populate/cell/structure/effect references.
Create/query/update pooled Cell state and transform.
Apply movement, combat, eat, animation, or interaction state.
Route to presentation and bounded event/message surfaces.

flows.description: CreatureData and rigblocks feed EditorData; editor tools mutate transient runtime and history; derived editor skin/model assets are produced for presentation, while authored save remains a separate asset boundary.

steps.action: Read creature-data/editor resource or model.
Mutate parts/colors/pose and commit transient history.
Build/paint skin meshes and material references.
Display editor creature/model through graphics state.

flows.description: Space generation creates star/planet records, binds EmpireData and colony state, updates relationships/economy/missions, and emits communication or message events. Generation and event order are static/inferred, not runtime-observed.

steps.action: Create/query star and planet records.
Bind empire, home world, colonies, and ownership.
Mutate relationship, mission, inventory, and trade state.
Create/queue/display communication state.

flows.description: Generated PlanetData supplies planet identity and terrain key; the live planet/terrain transition creates surface state; terrain and planet visual state feed presentation and editor modification surfaces.

steps.action: Select planet scores/species/ownership/generated terrain key.
Resolve cPlanet/cTerrainSphere and load terrain assets/state.
Apply terrain modifications and runtime updates.
Submit land/atmosphere/decal/planet presentation.

flows.description: Creature and Cell progression owners mutate progression, while SaveData captures mode-specific serializable candidates and restores them through a persistence manager. Exact handoff and synchronization are unresolved.

steps.action: Mutate evolution, Cell progression, missions, and counters.
Expose layout/interface to the persistence service.
Serialize/restore through ClassSerializer/PropertyList/owner interfaces.
Rehydrate runtime or progression owners after load.

flows.description: Game-mode manager exits the current mode, selects/activates the next mode, and invokes mode-owned runtime/presentation initialization and teardown. Cross-stage persistent state survival is intentionally unresolved.

steps.action: Hold mode-owned gameplay/presentation state.
Exit A and select B through SetActiveModeAt/messages.
Initialize/enter B services and state.
Determine what is reset, serialized, or rehydrated.

flows.description: Subsystem event records, messages, animation/editor events, and feedback events are dispatched through their own owners. The flow is intentionally variant-specific and does not create a universal event ABI.

steps.action: Create or post an event/listener request.
Store/select the event by ID/listener/priority semantics.
Dispatch to mode/editor/gameplay consumers.
Mutate owned mode, pose, effect, UI, or event state.

flows.description: IConfigManager/PropertyList/collectable and option configuration feeds bounded runtime/editor/content settings. Defaults and configuration migration are not inferred where absent.

steps.action: Load config/options/properties with evidenced fallbacks.
Mutate current option/property/collectable state.
Apply bounded configuration to Cell/editor/progression consumers.
Save preferences or reset to defaults only through named surfaces.

flows.description: The noun registry materializes a building, city state owns it, layout slots occupy placement, processing updates effectiveness, and removal releases layout/city/noun relationships. Exact costs, rollback, and full destruction order are unknown.

steps.action: Create/resolve building game-data subtype.
Append building and occupy layout slot.
Process connectivity/effectiveness and owner state.
Remove layout/city references and release instance.

central_data_structures.role: Resource identity plus database/factory/cache ownership; upstream of content and presentation loads.
Cross-mode noun/game-data identity, owner, political identity, factory, materialization, serialization, and refcount boundary.
Shared typed property/configuration/serialization substrate across editor, missions, inventory, scenario, and configuration.
Static Cell templates that feed world, spawn, combat, loot, effect, and model selection.
Live Cell mode state owner with pool, query, world refs, avatar, timing, and serializable pointer.
Mode-specific save candidate and progression boundary distinct from content and live entities.
Authored creature/editor model and rigblock graph feeding runtime creature, skin, and presentation conversion.
Political identity, star/planet records, colonies, relationship, inventory, trade, mission, and active-space context.
Downstream model/material/texture/world/effect/UI state; explicitly separated from gameplay predicates.
Variant-specific event records and the distinct App message transport used to coordinate listeners and mode/editor state.

provenance.purpose: Semantic schema/graph synthesis for data-model tracks 01-14.
provenance.method: Read-only synthesis from the fourteen committed research artifacts; no SPORE inspection, source/Ghidra/historical changes, runtime execution, or decompiled-source reproduction.
synthesis_rules: Separate template, runtime state, save state, configuration, and presentation even when the same field is copied between layers.
Use full type/group/instance identity semantically; do not serialize memory field order as graph order.
Include create/query/mutate/serialize/destroy only when an input artifact names or bounds the operation.
Keep analytical names such as WorldData, PlanetData, ProgressionData, EditorData, SaveData, and PresentationData distinct from literal recovered original types.
Do not infer a universal entity, event ABI, inheritance graph, save wire format, or runtime order where the inputs record conflicts or gaps.
Sort all graph arrays by stable id; source references are deterministic paths plus locators.

evidence_policy.static_is_not_runtime: VERIFIED layout/function/source evidence remains static unless an input explicitly says observed current behavior; original runtime order is not promoted.
evidence_policy.current_source_scope: OBSERVED_CURRENT applies only to current OpenSpore behavior and is comparison-only for the original.
evidence_policy.confidence: No numeric confidence was added; the bounded evidence level and explicit gap/limit text are preserved.

contradictions_preserved: The historical 0x00E4CE20 GetGlobalsData label conflicts with later teardown/correction evidence; this graph avoids using it as the canonical globals accessor.
Direct Cell content records are not automatically CellSerializer envelopes; Cell content and cCellSerializableData are separate layers.
ResourceKey conceptual identity and memory field order are not conflated.
SDK anchors are retained as bounded function surfaces where input artifacts report entry/body conflicts.
Property layout, cCellGlobalsResource/cCellSerializableData attribution, GMDL trailer, and no-RTTI limitations remain bounded contradictions/gaps.
The event family is not flattened into one universal event structure; message queue records and listener entries remain distinct.
